mechanism_narrative: Sustained four-week upward trend in WORKPLACES mobility (from -25.9% to -13.9%) signals progressive workplace reopening. This restores commuting routines and weekday retail visitation patterns, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 12 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the prior 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses by more than 5 percentage points in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility (10.6% above baseline) combined with suppressed RETAIL_REC (-21.9%) indicates consumers are sheltering in place. If RESIDENTIAL remains elevated while TRANSIT remains depressed, retail mobility will continue declining as consumers avoid public spaces.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 8% and TRANSIT remains below -20%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases by more than 3 percentage points in week t+1 while RESIDENTIAL remains above 8% and TRANSIT below -20%.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has remained consistently suppressed (range -30.7% to -29.0%) over four weeks, indicating outdoor recreation is constrained. This constraint prevents substitution away from indoor retail, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed as consumers lack alternative leisure outlets.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS mobility consistently below -29% for four consecutive weeks
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises above -20% in week t+1 and RETAIL_REC simultaneously increases by more than 5 percentage points.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains stable and elevated (11.6-12.7% above baseline) while RETAIL_REC is suppressed, indicating consumers are making essential trips but avoiding discretionary retail. If this bifurcation persists, RETAIL_REC will remain depressed as essential-only mobility patterns dominate.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 10% while RETAIL_REC remains below -20%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM converge within 5 percentage points, indicating resumption of discretionary shopping alongside essential trips.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved from -31.7% to -23.0% over four weeks, indicating partial restoration of public transport access. If TRANSIT continues this recovery trajectory and crosses above -15%, retail accessibility will improve sharply, driving RETAIL_REC upward within one week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -15% in week t+1
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 8.7 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: TRANSIT crosses above -15% but RETAIL_REC does not increase by at least 2 percentage points within the following week.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT show parallel recovery patterns (both improving 12-8.7 points respectively), suggesting coordinated reopening of economic activity. This synchronized recovery will amplify retail footfall through both commuting and workplace-adjacent shopping, driving RETAIL_REC higher over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve by >5 points week-on-week simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 12 points, TRANSIT improved 8.7 points over four weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT do not both improve in the same week, or RETAIL_REC declines despite synchronized improvement in both proxies.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from 16.4% to 10.6% over four weeks, indicating gradual return to normal activity patterns outside the home. This sustained decline in sheltering-in-place behavior will continue, releasing suppressed retail demand and driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 5.8 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility reverses and increases by more than 2 percentage points in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC does not increase despite continued RESIDENTIAL decline.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved from -32.3% to -21.9% over four weeks (10.4 point gain), establishing a clear recovery trend. If this linear improvement continues at the same rate, RETAIL_REC will reach -11.5% by week t+4, representing sustained upward momentum independent of other factors.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 10.4 percentage points over four weeks at consistent rate
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines by more than 2 percentage points in week t+1, breaking the four-week upward trend, or the mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than the prior 28-day mean.
